candidates.title: Apparatus to remove a disposable cloth from a hand operated flat mop through a single trigger mechanism without having to touch the disposable cloth

timeline.event: No reinstatement listed in Gazette issues 2024-11-12 to 2026-11-03

technical.summary: The patent claims a hand-operated flat mop apparatus featuring a trigger mechanism to release a disposable cloth without manual contact. The device comprises a top plate, a push plate with spikes or hooks, a mechanical plate, linkages, ratchet collars, and compression springs. Activating the trigger allows spring force to move the push plate, releasing the cloth.
technical.mechanism: Mechanical trigger mechanism utilizing compression springs and linkages to release cloth
key_claim_elements: A flat mop having a handle and apparatus for retaining the handle to a top plate of the flat mop
a top plate including a first cover member and a second cover member
a push plate having a top surface which contains thereon along a first side a multiplicity of groups of spaced apart spikes
a mechanical plate with openings to receive the pair of ratchet collars and a pair of spring housings
a trigger mechanism
a first compression spring and a second compression spring
quotes: A flat mop having a handle and apparatus for retaining the handle to a top plate of the flat mop
when the trigger is activated, a downward force of the springs cause the push plate to move away from the mechanical plate and the micro-fiber cloth is released from the spikes and is released

when the trigger is activated, a downward force of the springs cause the push plate to move away from the mechanical plate and the non-woven cloth is pulled away from the hook retaining members and is released

opportunity.rationale: The patent describes a trigger mechanism for releasing disposable cloths on a flat mop without manual contact, which aligns directly with the intended product category of non-powered household cleaning tools. The mechanism relies on mechanical linkages, springs, and plates rather than electronics, fitting the small manufacturer constraint. However, the assembly of ratchet collars and compression springs requires higher precision than static mop heads. The expired status due to non-payment suggests the original owner did not realize sufficient return on investment, possibly due to manufacturing costs or consumer adoption issues. For a new entrant, this removes licensing barriers but does not eliminate the production complexity that may have hindered the original owner. The technology is free to use, but the cost-benefit ratio of the mechanical complexity must be validated against simpler attachment methods.

candidates.title: Devices and methods for dispensing fluids and wiping surfaces

timeline.event: No reinstatement listed in Gazette issues 2024-11-12 to 2026-11-03

technical.summary: The patent claims a cleaning device configured to selectively dispense a fluid to a surface being cleaned. The device includes a housing where the outer portion is "configured to be grasped and manipulated by a user during a cleaning procedure" [9f5af1b5d8ca]. It comprises "a dispenser comprising a porous or fluid permeable material" [9f5af1b5d8ca] and "a wiper removably attached to the wiper portion of the outer housing portion" [9f5af1b5d8ca]. The wiper is repositionable "to enable a different portion of the outer fabric layer to comprise the wiping surface" [9f5af1b5d8ca]. No motor, battery, or power source is claimed.
key_claim_elements: housing comprising an outer housing portion and an inner housing portion
dispenser comprising a porous or fluid permeable material
wiper removably attached to the wiper portion of the outer housing portion
quotes: configured to be grasped and manipulated by a user during a cleaning procedure
a dispenser comprising a porous or fluid permeable material
a wiper removably attached to the wiper portion of the outer housing portion
to enable a different portion of the outer fabric layer to comprise the wiping surface

challenges: Confirming absolute expiration status across all jurisdictions
Ensuring no active continuations or divisionals exist
opportunity.rationale: The patent covers a manual cleaning device configured to dispense fluid and wipe surfaces, aligning directly with the intended product category of non-powered household cleaning tools [9f5af1b5d8ca]. The claims describe a housing grasped by a user and a wiper removably attached to the outer housing portion, which matches the design constraints for manual mops or scrubbers [9f5af1b5d8ca]. The inclusion of a dispenser with porous material suggests a specific mechanism for fluid delivery that is commercially desirable in modern cleaning tools [9f5af1b5d8ca]. Engineering effort is moderate as the device requires no motor, battery, or power source, but does involve mechanical design for fluid dispensing and repositionable wiper attachment [9f5af1b5d8ca]. Regarding maintenance fees, the owner's decision to stop payments usually indicates the patent was worth little to them. This does apply to a new entrant in terms of reduced legal risk, as the technology is likely in the public domain. However, the low value to the original owner may not apply to a new entrant who can integrate these features into a broader product line where fluid dispensing and reversible wipers are standard consumer expectations, providing value through product completeness rather than exclusive monopoly rights.

technical.summary: The patent discloses "A height adjustment lock system comprising: a braking cylinder for receiving an upper pole section and a lower pole section" [8dd7d8547c94]. The system utilizes "the locking handle comprises a brake shoe pusher that protrudes inward from the generally cylindrical inner surface and is capable of applying force to the brake shoe when the locking handle is moved downward toward the lower pole section" [8dd7d8547c94]. The invention may be embodied in "A height adjustable cleaning device comprising: a pole comprising a lower pole section and an upper pole section; a cleaning head attached to the lower pole section" [8dd7d8547c94].

brake shoe
locking handle
brake shoe pusher
quotes: A height adjustment lock system comprising: a braking cylinder for receiving an upper pole section and a lower pole section

the locking handle comprises a brake shoe pusher that protrudes inward from the generally cylindrical inner surface and is capable of applying force to the brake shoe when the locking handle is moved downward toward the lower pole section
A height adjustable cleaning device comprising: a pole comprising a lower pole section and an upper pole section; a cleaning head attached to the lower pole section

opportunity.rationale: The patent discloses a height adjustment lock system specifically for cleaning devices comprising a pole and cleaning head [8dd7d8547c94]. This aligns directly with the intended product category of manual cleaning tools like mops. The mechanism involves a braking cylinder and locking handle with a brake shoe pusher [8dd7d8547c94], offering a specific mechanical solution for pole adjustment common in this category. As the patent is expired due to nonpayment, the technology is in the public domain, removing licensing barriers for a small manufacturer. The original owner's decision to stop paying fees suggests the specific implementation may not have provided sufficient competitive advantage or margin to justify the cost at their scale. However, for a new entrant, the zero licensing cost allows integration of a potentially superior locking mechanism without IP risk, differentiating the product from basic fixed-height or simpler friction-lock competitors. The engineering effort is moderate as it requires manufacturing specific mechanical components like brake shoes and cylinders rather than simple snap-fits, but fits within non-powered manufacturing capabilities.

prose.executive_summary: The run looked at 2404 US utility patents in the cleaning-tool CPC groups. 299 of them appear in Official Gazette expiration notices from the last 104 weeks, 209 passed the non-powered screen and 8 were analysed. Recommended for technical and legal review: US 8,800,092 (Apparatus to remove a disposable cloth from a hand operated flat mop through a single trigger mechanism without having to touch the disposable cloth), US 10,052,665 (Devices and methods for dispensing fluids and wiping surfaces). Every status is dated and comes from public notices; none of this is legal clearance.
prose.methodology: The search began with a CPC code query. This returned 2404 candidates. The Gazette was checked for expired patents and reinstatements. This found 299 candidates that expired in the relevant window. A non-powered screen was run on all candidates. This left 209 candidates. The status of these candidates was verified. This left 210 candidates. The candidates were ranked. The top 8 candidates were analysed. 201 candidates were not analysed. 2 candidates were recommended.
prose.commercial:
All candidates align with the intended product category of non-powered household cleaning tools. US 8,800,092 and US 10,052,665 receive Shortlist recommendations while the others receive Hold recommendations. US 8,800,092 describes a trigger mechanism for releasing disposable cloths. The assembly involves ratchet collars and compression springs. This requires higher precision than static mop heads. US 10,052,665 covers a manual cleaning device configured to dispense fluid. The inclusion of a dispenser with porous material matches design constraints for manual mops. Engineering effort for both is moderate as neither requires a motor or battery.

The Hold candidates involve different mechanical systems. US 10,052,751 discloses a height adjustment lock system involving a braking cylinder. US 8,826,487 claims a mop cleaning set with a dehydration device. Both require mechanical design and tooling for plastic components. US 8,826,487 carries a flag for a related active continuation. US 10,065,611 claims a windshield cleaning implement with an arcuate shaft. The specific automotive application limits direct relevance to a general household cleaning product line compared to the floor cleaning focus of the other candidates. All five patents list expired status due to nonpayment.
prose.next_steps: For US 8,800,092, verify the mechanical complexity of the trigger mechanism. Assess manufacturing feasibility and costs. For US 10,052,665, evaluate the fluid dispensing mechanism. Confirm compatibility with intended cleaning solutions. Check wiper attachment mechanisms for durability and ease of use.

methodology: Search: CPC prefixes for non-powered household cleaning tools (A47L 13, A47L 1, A47L 17, A47K 11/10 and related groups).
Status source: Official Gazette notices, 104 weekly issues fetched out of 104 requested.
Screening: powered co-classes removed, power terms in independent claims removed, unclear cases flagged.
Status rules: a later official notice wins; expired means listed as expired with no later reinstatement found.
Scoring: commercial relevance 35%, engineering effort 20% (inverted), evidence quality 25%, unresolved risk 20% (inverted).
key_assumptions: The Gazette scan is current to the issue of 2026-11-03; expirations appear about eight weeks after the anniversary.
PatentsView bibliographic data ends with grants of 2021-09-28 and claims with grants of October 2019.
Patent term adjustment is not available in public tables, so end-of-term dates are estimates.
quality_of_information: Official Gazette notices are the USPTO's own publication (grade A).
EPO OPS cross-check: not configured for this run, so each status rests on one official source
201 eligible candidates were not analysed because of the analysis cap.
limitations: US patents only; nothing here speaks to other countries.
Screening only. Related patents, design patents and trade dress may still cover a product.
A lapsed patent can be reinstated later; intervening rights protect only use that began during the lapse.
Terminal disclaimers are checked only where PatentsView records them.
No independent second source for status; the EPO OPS registration was pending.
